reason: Verified in source and by driving. lately.html:713-737 builds .page as header.top > main > div.coverage, and every ancestor of that div is a plain div (div.coverage > div.page > div.scroll > div.canvas > div.app > div#root > body), so it is inside no sectioning content and no landmark. Playwright's ARIA snapshot of the rendered page at 1440x960 confirms it: the tree contains banner and main and nothing else, and a text-node walk finds 'Tasks / answered', 'Timeline / answered', 'Notes / answered, for you', 'Read 09:14, Thursday 16 July 2026' and the Lab provenance sentence all sitting outside main, header, nav, footer and aside. The same orphan holds in full, partial, quiet, first-run, empty, loading and error, because shell() is the single template for all seven. The seat's own sibling proves the inconsistency rather than mere taste: header.top at the identical depth already maps to banner, so the coverage strip is the one top-level block in .page that opted out of the landmark model. Neither gate covers this - audit.mjs has no landmark or tag assertions at all, and interaction-check.mjs touches .coverage only via a class selector at lines 261 and 281-282 to read its text - so this is not a restatement of anything already proven. I do trim the consequence: content outside a landmark is still announced in ordinary browse-mode reading, so the strip is not unreachable; what it is missing from is landmark navigation (NVDA D, VoiceOver rotor), 'skip to main content', and reader-mode/main-content extraction, which is a real structural fault and not nothing. That is why I correct the class upward: the seat filed refinement, and refinement means nothing is wrong. Something is wrong here - it is invisible to sighted users but it is a genuine structural defect - so this is a defect, not a refinement. The proposed fix is correct as written and its numbers hold. I applied it live: replacing the div with <footer class="coverage t-label" data-type="label" aria-label="What this reading was built from"> yields a contentinfo landmark named 'What this reading was built from' (contentinfo maps because no sectioning-content ancestor exists), and the rect is byte-identical before and after - x 206, y 1776.375, width 1084, height 50.6875 - with display flex, margin-top 48px, padding-top 16px and the 1px top border all preserved, since the class carries the layout and footer's only UA default is display:block, which .coverage overrides. Re-checked at 390, 768 and 1280: heights 133, 84 and 51, display flex, margin-top 48px, unchanged from the div. No CSS change is needed, exactly as claimed.
sharpenedFix: Take the fix as proposed, with two constraints on how it lands. Keep the <footer> a direct child of .page, a sibling after </main> - moving it inside <main> or inside a <section> would demote it to a generic footer with no landmark role and silently undo the whole fix. And make the edit inside shell() only, which is the one template feeding all seven states, so no state is left with the bare div. If this pattern is later ported into the real /app/home/analytics route rather than this standalone master, check first whether the surrounding app shell already emits a contentinfo; two contentinfo landmarks on one page is worse than none, and in that case the strip should become <section aria-label="What this reading was built from"> (a named region landmark) instead of a footer.
breaks: Nothing measurable. Both behaviour-gate references to this element - interaction-check.mjs:261 and :281-282 - select by .coverage class, not by tag, so they keep passing; the strip's text content and its coverage of the source that did not answer are untouched. The 'main section', 'main p' and 'main button' counts at interaction-check.mjs:359 and :382-384 are unaffected because the strip sits outside main both before and after. audit.mjs asserts nothing about tags or landmarks, and the palette, weight, family, contrast, hit-target, radius, motion, type-ramp and leading checks all key off the unchanged class and data-type="label". After it lands, re-run both gates, and re-capture the seven light frames plus 390/768/1280 to confirm the rect is unmoved - the live substitution says it is identical, but the frames are the record. One thing genuinely changes and should be listened to rather than only looked at: the strip now announces as a named contentinfo, so confirm the label reads as intended in the reading order and that no second contentinfo has appeared.
